images.filename: Fifth Avenue Theatre interior, Seattle, ca 1926 (MOHAI 1172).jpg
images.caption:
Audiences were fascinated with the decor of the new Fifth Avenue Theatre. Its brightly-painted woodwork had been inspired by traditional Chinese decorated wood structures in Beijing's Forbidden City. The Asian theme was in keeping with Seattle's position as a gateway for Pacific trade.
Handwritten on sleeve: Fifth Ave Theatre Interior Decorations.

Caption by MOHAI staff.

images.filename: Box office at the new Fifth Avenue Theatre, September 24, 1926 (MOHAI 5793).jpg
images.caption:
The Fifth Avenue Theatre first opened to an exclusive group of guests on September 23, 1924. All of the detail in its elaborate decor, from the box office to the auditorium ceiling, had a Chinese theme. The Seattle Post-Intelligencer noted that it "cast the mystic spell of a Chinese temple of a thousand years ago."
This photo, taken at the 1924 opening, shows the box office with its silk curtains and its lacquer and marble facade. Admission was 65 to 85 cents for adults and 25 cents for children.

Subjects (LCTGM): Theaters; Fifth Avenue Theatre (Seattle, Wash.)

images.filename: Grand opening of the 5th Avenue Theatre, September 24, 1926 (MOHAI 5885).jpg
images.caption:
The 5th Avenue Theatre opened on September 24, 1926. It was located between Union and University Streets and featured movies and performing acts.
In this photo, spotlights shine on the front of the building, as a crowd gathers for opening night. Admission to the opening was 65 cents for adults and 25 cents for children.
